title: Another school's Abhidharma
hook: the Sarvastivada school had its own Abhidharma, summarized by Vasubandhu

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Kathavatthu, the book of debates with other early schools. Your line: points of controversy. Did you say someone's point back in their words before giving yours? Day one thousand ninety-one.

Yesterday's book argued with other schools without naming them. One of those schools had a name that is itself a claim: Sarvastivada, the teaching that all exists. And it didn't only argue. It built its own Abhidharma, its own books, its own lists of what the world is made of. For weeks now this path has been learning one map of the mind. Today, a second map, drawn by people studying the same teacher, with the same care, from a different starting point.
screen: `THE TEACHING THAT ALL EXISTS.` → `ITS OWN BOOKS, ITS OWN LISTS.` → `A SECOND MAP.`

segments.voice: The Sarvastivadins held that the basic building blocks of experience, which they called dharmas, exist in the past, the present and the future, not only in this moment. That's where the name comes from. It let them explain how a past deed can still bear fruit, or how memory reaches something gone. The Theravada side, as yesterday's book shows, answered that the past is past. Both were working from the Buddha's words. This school's Abhidharma was gathered and argued over at length, and then summed up by a monk named Vasubandhu in a book of verses called the Abhidharmakosha, the treasury of Abhidharma. Then something unusual. Vasubandhu also wrote his own commentary on those verses, and in it, at points, he raises objections to the very school he was summarizing, at times speaking for another group, the Sautrantikas. A textbook that argues with itself in the margins. Now put the two lists side by side. The Theravada manual sorts everything into four: mind, mental factors, matter, and nibbana. The Treasury sorts it into five groups: matter, mind, mental factors, a group of things that are neither matter nor mind, and the unconditioned. One small example of how the lists differ: space. In the Theravada manual, space is counted as a kind of matter, the gap that marks where one thing ends. In the Treasury, space is listed among the unconditioned. Same space. Two careful answers. The Treasury has been studied in other Buddhist traditions too, tradition says. Neither list is a rough draft of the other. They're two schools looking hard at the same world.
screen: `ALL EXISTS: PAST, PRESENT, FUTURE.` · `VASUBANDHU'S TREASURY.` · `FOUR GROUPS AND FIVE.` · then, large: `SAME SPACE, TWO ANSWERS.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice, if you'd like: compare two lists without judging. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind two ways of doing the same ordinary thing: two people you know who load a dishwasher differently, or pack a bag, or set a table. Hold both pictures side by side. Notice what each one gets right. When the mind starts to pick a winner, notice that too, and set it down. Just let the two sit next to each other, both whole. The bell holds the time.
Another school's Abhidharma. The Sarvastivada map of mind and matter, summed up in Vasubandhu's Treasury, sorting the world into five groups. Today's word.
Your line: another school's list. Today, when you meet a way of doing things that isn't yours, find one thing it sees that yours doesn't, before you decide anything. Day one thousand ninety-one.

howItsDone: Students of Buddhist philosophy read Vasubandhu's Treasury of Abhidharma alongside the Theravada manuals, and some Mahayana monastic curricula include it as a core text.

fork.setup: you're Vasubandhu. you've written verses summing up a school's Abhidharma. now you sit down to write your own commentary on them. what do you do?
options: at points, raise objections to the school you summarized
fork.reveal: his commentary at points argues with the very school his verses summarize, at times from the Sautrantika side: a textbook arguing in its own margins.

original.note: Sanskrit: the teaching that all exists, the name of an early Buddhist school with its own Abhidharma.

trapdoor: what you thought: Abhidharma is one book everyone agreed on.
what it means: more than one school built its own Abhidharma; the Sarvastivada list sorts the world into five groups, not four.
what a scholar hears: Vasubandhu's Abhidharmakosha and its auto-commentary, which at points criticizes the Vaibhashika view from a Sautrantika position.

sources.ref: Vasubandhu, Abhidharmakosha and its bhashya (auto-commentary), chapter I (the five groups of dharmas) and chapter V (the debate on past and future)
Abhidhammattha Sangaha I and VI (the four ultimate realities; space as a kind of matter)
Kathavatthu I.6 (the debate on whether all exists)

notes: Hook says 'for weeks now this path has been learning one map of the mind' (Block A began at day 1062).
Sarvastivada as 'the teaching that all exists' and the reasons given (past deeds bearing fruit, memory of the past) follow Abhidharmakosha V; confirm.
Vasubandhu's auto-commentary criticizing Vaibhashika positions from a Sautrantika view: standard scholarly account; phrased 'at times'. No dates given.
Five groups in the Kosha (rupa, citta, caitta, cittaviprayukta-samskara, asamskrta) vs the four paramattha of the Sangaha; confirm.
Space (akasa-dhatu) as limiting matter among the 28 in Sangaha VI, and akasa among the three unconditioned in the Kosha; confirm.
'The Treasury went on to be studied in other Buddhist traditions' and howItsDone's 'some Mahayana monastic curricula' (e.g. Tibetan colleges): confirm or soften.
The Theravada and Sarvastivada positions are set side by side without ranking, per the practice.
